notes: Mixed-constructive, not full risk-on. Goldman Sachs: resilient growth, AI capex and earnings support risk assets, but flags a more fragmented/multipolar equity market (opportunity in small/mid-caps and international, not just US mega-cap) and rising AI-related debt as a credit risk to watch. JPMorgan: stocks are supported by AI-capex-driven earnings rather than broad economic strength; base case has US high-grade credit spreads moving sideways-to-modestly-wider through H2 2026 (85bp -> 95bp target), which is a late-cycle caution signal, not a reflation all-clear. DBS: Fed funds seen settling near 3% by end-2026 (further gradual cuts), and Singapore banks (DBS/OCBC/UOB) were upgraded to Overweight on stronger NII/NIM and dividend growth -- directly relevant to this portfolio's SG core holdings (D05, O39). Net read: growth/earnings momentum still supports a modest tilt toward the satellite (momentum) sleeve, but the credit-spread and AI-debt caution argues against a large tilt -- kept deliberately modest (+/-5%) rather than aggressive, since conviction here is mixed, not high.
